definitions.explanation: A cord, string, or strap used to attach, tie, or fasten something. Commonly refers to the thong of a sandal or the chin strap of a hat.

examples.japanese: {下駄|げた}の{緒|お}が{切|き}れた。
examples.english: The thong of my wooden sandal broke.

examples.japanese: {草履|ぞうり}の{緒|お}を{付|つ}け{替|か}える。
examples.english: I'll replace the strap on my zori sandals.

examples.japanese: {帽子|ぼうし}の{緒|お}を{顎|あご}の{下|した}で{結|むす}んだ。
examples.english: I tied the chin strap of the hat under my chin.

notes:
An old and fundamental Japanese word for a cord or strap used to fasten things. Most commonly encountered in connection with traditional Japanese footwear.

COMMON COMPOUNDS:
- {鼻緒|はなお}: the thong/strap of a sandal (geta, zori, etc.)
- {帯緒|おびお}: a cord used to secure an obi
- {手綱|たづな}: reins (literally "hand cord")

USAGE:
- In modern Japanese, {緒|お} as a standalone word is somewhat literary or traditional
- The compound {鼻緒|はなお} is the most common modern usage
- Also appears in the set expression {戦|いくさ}の{緒|お}に{就|つ}く — to enter battle

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {緒|お}が{切|き}れる: a strap breaks
- {緒|お}を{結|むす}ぶ: to tie a cord
- {緒|お}を{付|つ}ける: to attach a strap

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {紐|ひも}: string, cord — the general everyday word for any cord or string
- {鼻緒|はなお}: sandal thong — the most common compound using {緒|お}
- {帯|おび}: sash, belt — worn around the waist with kimono
